assessor: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Claude Code), 2026-10-19. Advisory, same provider family as the author. Written for the 43 Verbal Reasoning and Reading items the text-length estimator would block. It is NOT the independent difficulty evidence for these sections: the different-provider reviewer's difficulty rating is. Same method as the 35: reasoning steps, rule given or discovered, trap or search; marks not used.

scholarship-y6-vr-003.label: easy
scholarship-y6-vr-003.rationale: Tool-to-user analogy with a single clear relation.

scholarship-y6-vr-004.label: medium
scholarship-y6-vr-004.rationale: The relation is 'a lack of', and the near-miss HUNGER (a result, not the lack) has to be rejected.

scholarship-y6-vr-010.label: medium
scholarship-y6-vr-010.rationale: Four artworks and one tool; the category has to be named before the odd one is seen. Borderline easy.

scholarship-y6-vr-011.label: medium
scholarship-y6-vr-011.rationale: Needs DWINDLE, RECEDE and DIMINISH to be known as decline words. Vocabulary, not reasoning load. Borderline easy.

scholarship-y6-vr-012.label: medium
scholarship-y6-vr-012.rationale: Declared challenging. It tests knowing that bronze, brass, steel and pewter are alloys and copper is an element; the knowledge is specific but the reasoning is one step.

scholarship-y6-vr-014.label: medium
scholarship-y6-vr-014.rationale: PRUDENT is above everyday Year 6 vocabulary; the reasoning is a single synonym match.

scholarship-y6-vr-015.label: medium
scholarship-y6-vr-015.rationale: DISCLOSE is the only unfamiliar word; the task is one antonym match.

scholarship-y6-vr-019.label: medium
scholarship-y6-vr-019.rationale: FRUGAL and EXTRAVAGANT are both above everyday range; THRIFTY, STINGY and CAREFUL are plausible same-direction distractors.

scholarship-y6-vr-021.label: easy
scholarship-y6-vr-021.rationale: NEWSPAPER and PAPERWEIGHT are both common compounds; trying the options in turn finds it quickly.

scholarship-y6-vr-022.label: medium
scholarship-y6-vr-022.rationale: Two senses of one word have to be held at once and matched.

scholarship-y6-vr-023.label: medium
scholarship-y6-vr-023.rationale: Two senses of POST, both familiar.

scholarship-y6-vr-024.label: challenging
scholarship-y6-vr-024.rationale: The second sense of SOUND (a strait) is rare for this age, so the item turns on knowledge a strong candidate may simply not have.

scholarship-y6-vr-028.label: medium
scholarship-y6-vr-028.rationale: Contrapositive reasoning ('it did not open, so it did not snow'); the trap options affirm the consequent.

scholarship-y6-vr-029.label: easy
scholarship-y6-vr-029.rationale: Direct application of a universal rule.

scholarship-y6-vr-030.label: easy
scholarship-y6-vr-030.rationale: Disjunctive syllogism with a plain 'either or'.

scholarship-y6-vr-031.label: challenging
scholarship-y6-vr-031.rationale: Three statements, a contrapositive through a chain, and a conclusion that is about the negative. Borderline medium.

scholarship-y6-vr-035.label: medium
scholarship-y6-vr-035.rationale: Declared challenging. A, D, I, P are the letters at square-number positions: one idea, widely met in puzzle books, and checkable by the growing differences 3, 5, 7.

scholarship-y6-vr-038.label: easy
scholarship-y6-vr-038.rationale: Each pair moves up four letters; the pattern is visible from the first two terms.

scholarship-y6-vr-039.label: medium
scholarship-y6-vr-039.rationale: A steady step of three but the series wraps past Z, adding a step.

scholarship-y6-vr-041.label: easy
scholarship-y6-vr-041.rationale: The shift is shown by one worked example; applying it in reverse is one step.

scholarship-y6-vr-042.label: medium
scholarship-y6-vr-042.rationale: Two examples must be combined to read an unfamiliar substitution; no single shift.

scholarship-y6-rc-004.label: easy
scholarship-y6-rc-004.rationale: Answer is stated: the young fish 'sought sanctuary'.

scholarship-y6-rc-008.label: medium
scholarship-y6-rc-008.rationale: Tone has to be inferred across the whole passage.

scholarship-y6-rc-010.label: easy
scholarship-y6-rc-010.rationale: Literal retrieval from paragraph 2 (now with tentative wording).

scholarship-y6-rc-015.label: medium
scholarship-y6-rc-015.rationale: Requires linking the root-network sentence to a consequence not stated outright.

scholarship-y6-rc-016.label: medium
scholarship-y6-rc-016.rationale: Summarising the author's view from a closing sentence needs a little abstraction.

scholarship-y6-rc-017.label: easy
scholarship-y6-rc-017.rationale: Literal link between curled leaves and lost water.

scholarship-y6-rc-018.label: easy
scholarship-y6-rc-018.rationale: Meaning is given by the next phrase in the same sentence. Borderline medium.

scholarship-y6-rc-019.label: easy
scholarship-y6-rc-019.rationale: Main-argument item whose argument is stated in the opening and closing paragraphs. Borderline medium.

scholarship-y6-rc-026.label: medium
scholarship-y6-rc-026.rationale: Purpose of a detail: the candidate must infer why the author mentions it, not find it.

scholarship-y6-rc-028.label: easy
scholarship-y6-rc-028.rationale: Literal: winds allowed faster speeds. Long options, simple retrieval.

scholarship-y6-rc-031.label: easy
scholarship-y6-rc-031.rationale: The term is defined by the dash clause in the same paragraph.
